subject: Literature
title: Roman Satire and Social Commentary
description: A quick, practical guide to Roman Satire and Social Commentary.

hook.text: While Roman emperors demanded praise, poets like Juvenal mocked the powerful in verses read across the empire.

buildup.text: Roman satire attacked corruption, greed, and hypocrisy using humor, irony, and exaggeration.

discovery.text: Juvenal coined phrases still used today, including 'bread and circuses' to describe political distraction.

twist.text: Despite their wit, satirists risked exile or death if their targets had enough political power to retaliate.

climax.text: Roman satire established the tradition of using humor to speak truth to power that persists in literature.

punchline.text: Ancient comedians risked their lives to mock the powerful.

quiz.question: What phrase did the Roman satirist Juvenal coin?
options: When in Rome, do as the Romans
